surfaceForm: University of Luxembourg / the University (as a named, specific institution)
location: main-body-EN.tex — passim, first at "Summary for stakeholders" (l.19) and "Reading guide" (l.456), "Introduction" (l.691), "NIS2 Directive: the University as an essential entity" (l.1044)
proposedGenericDecision: Refer to the adopting institution by role: "the University" / "the institution" / "the adopting research-and-teaching university". Drop the proper name; keep the generic class (research-and-teaching university, NIS2 essential entity).
rationale: The proper name 'University of Luxembourg' appears dozens of times and is the single largest barrier to institution-agnostic reuse. Role-based reference ('the University') already coexists in the text and can absorb every occurrence.

surfaceForm: uni.lu (implied institutional domain in eduroam/identity discussion; concrete /16 examples elsewhere are about Cambridge)
location: main-body-EN.tex — "Implement federated identity" (Proposition 10, l.4097) and identity sections
proposedGenericDecision: Use INSTITUTION_NREN_FEDERATION placeholder rather than any specific national federation; no concrete domain literal needed.
rationale: No literal uni.lu string is hard-coded, but identity/federation passages presuppose the institution's own domain. Flag for completeness; low confidence because no surface literal needs replacement.

surfaceForm: RESTENA (Luxembourg NREN) — "RESTENA national research-and-education network", "RESTENA-CSIRT", "RESTENA-operated Luxembourg identity federation"
location: main-body-EN.tex — "The academic domain in five minutes" (l.497), "Reference panel" (l.2055), "Luxembourg status" (l.2726-2750), NREN section (l.2661), "Shared Security Organizations" (l.3736), Proposition 10 (l.4098)
proposedGenericDecision: Replace with role 'the national NREN' / 'the institution's NREN' and 'the NREN CSIRT'. Keep GEANT (pan-European, jurisdiction-neutral) as the backbone reference.
rationale: RESTENA is the Luxembourg-specific NREN; the architectural argument ('connects to GEANT backbone, provides eduroam/eduGAIN, runs a CSIRT') is fully generic. Every NREN (RENATER, SWITCH, DFN, Jisc) provides the same primitives, so a role-based variable preserves the argument across jurisdictions.

surfaceForm: ILR — Institut Luxembourgeois de Régulation (national NIS2 supervisory authority); "the ILR", "classified by the ILR", "annual maturity report addressed to the ILR"
location: main-body-EN.tex — Board message (l.52), Luxembourg context (l.569), "NIS2 Directive" (l.1041-1048), "Supervisory authority and incident-response chain" (l.1117), Position D/B (l.1424, l.1506), Propositions 2/14 (l.4048, l.4120), Transition plan (l.3887, l.3925)
proposedGenericDecision: Replace with role 'the national NIS2 supervisory authority' / 'the competent authority'. The classification, audit, and annual-maturity-report obligations are NIS2-generic, not Luxembourg-specific.
rationale: ILR is the designated Luxembourg supervisory body; every Member State designates one under NIS2. The obligations (proactive supervision, audits, annual maturity report) flow from the Directive, so the role-based reference is fully transposable.

surfaceForm: GOVCERT.LU — governmental CSIRT; "the operational CSIRT for the University", "University reports incidents primarily through GOVCERT.LU"
location: main-body-EN.tex — Luxembourg context (l.574), "Supervisory authority and incident-response chain" (l.1122-1128), "Shared Security Organizations" (l.3733-3747), FIRST list (l.3747)
proposedGenericDecision: Replace with role 'the national governmental CSIRT' / 'the public-sector CSIRT of competent jurisdiction'.
rationale: GOVCERT.LU is the Luxembourg governmental CSIRT for public bodies. The incident-reporting-chain logic (public institution reports first-line to the national governmental CSIRT) is generic to most EU states; role substitution preserves it.

surfaceForm: HCPN — Haut-Commissariat à la Protection nationale; "hosts GOVCERT.LU and ANSSI Luxembourg", "single point of contact for cross-border NIS2 cooperation"
location: main-body-EN.tex — Luxembourg context (l.574), "Supervisory authority and incident-response chain" (l.1128), MONARC (l.2922), Position B.1/D (l.1425, l.1506, l.1530)
proposedGenericDecision: Replace with role 'the national single point of contact for NIS2 cooperation' / 'the national security authority hosting the governmental CSIRT'.
rationale: HCPN is the Luxembourg body that hosts the CSIRT and acts as the NIS2 single point of contact. NIS2 requires every state to designate a SPOC; the structural role transposes directly.

surfaceForm: ANSSI Luxembourg (ANSSI-LU) — national Agency for Information Systems Security; publishes PSI-LU; "distinct from the French ANSSI"
location: main-body-EN.tex — Luxembourg context (l.575), "Public-sector reference framework" (l.1189-1192), Position D (l.1506, l.1531)
proposedGenericDecision: Replace with role 'the national information-security agency'. Drop the French-ANSSI disambiguation note (artefact of the LU/FR collision).
rationale: ANSSI-LU is jurisdiction-specific; its role (authoring the public-sector information-security policy) is generic. The 'distinct from French ANSSI' clause is pure local-collision housekeeping that becomes meaningless once generalized.

surfaceForm: PSI-LU — Politique générale de la sécurité de l'information de l'État luxembourgeois (public-sector infosec baseline, approved 13 July 2018)
location: main-body-EN.tex — Luxembourg context (l.576), Methodology note (l.994), "Public-sector reference framework" (l.1186-1198)
proposedGenericDecision: Replace with role 'the national public-sector information-security baseline policy'. Keep the generic claim that the multi-zone architecture is a compatible operational implementation of the applicable public-sector baseline.
rationale: PSI-LU is the Luxembourg State infosec policy; most jurisdictions have an equivalent public-sector baseline. The architecture's positioning as 'a compatible implementation of the national baseline' is the generic, reusable claim.

surfaceForm: SERIMA — SEcurity RIsk MAnagement national notification platform; "single national incident-notification platform", "operated by the ILR in partnership with Luxembourg House of Cybersecurity, CNPD and HCPN", binding 24h/72h/30-day cadence
location: main-body-EN.tex — Luxembourg context (l.580), "Notification platform: SERIMA" (l.1144-1154), obligations tables (l.1282, l.1289, l.1368), MONARC (l.2927), Transition plan (l.3889, l.3926)
proposedGenericDecision: Replace platform name with role 'the national incident-notification platform'. Keep the NIS2 24h/72h/30-day cadence (it is Directive Art.23, jurisdiction-neutral); drop the May-2025 operational date and the LU operator list.
rationale: SERIMA is the Luxembourg platform; the 24/72/30 cadence is the binding NIS2 norm everywhere. The MONARC-as-risk-module integration and 2-May-2025 go-live are LU-specific and should drop or parameterize.

surfaceForm: MONARC — Luxembourg-developed risk-analysis method/tool (NC3 / Luxembourg House of Cybersecurity); "Luxembourg-developed methodology", integrated into SERIMA
location: main-body-EN.tex — "MONARC: Luxembourg risk-analysis methodology" (l.2918-2936), Five-element summary (l.628), Position B.3/D.2 (l.1444, l.1525), Propositions 14 (l.4122), Transition plan (l.3891)
proposedGenericDecision: Present MONARC as one example among open risk-analysis methodologies; lead with the jurisdiction-neutral ISO/IEC 27005 and offer MONARC as 'where a national open-source risk-analysis tool exists'. Drop 'Luxembourg-developed ... specific operational and political relevance'.
rationale: MONARC is genuinely useful and ISO-27005-aligned, but the section frames it as carrying 'specific operational and political relevance' for Luxembourg. Generalizing to ISO/IEC 27005 (already cited as the alternative) keeps the maturity-dashboard argument intact while MONARC becomes an optional national instantiation.

surfaceForm: CNPD — Commission nationale pour la protection des données (Luxembourg DPA)
location: main-body-EN.tex — SERIMA operator list (l.1149), Position D.5 (l.1555), Safeguards advocacy (l.3112)
proposedGenericDecision: Replace with role 'the national data-protection authority' / 'the competent supervisory authority under GDPR Art.51'.
rationale: CNPD is the Luxembourg DPA; every Member State has one under GDPR. Role substitution preserves the 'share register template with the DPA and EDPB' advocacy point.

surfaceForm: CIRCL — Luxembourg CSIRT for private sector / communes / NGOs
location: main-body-EN.tex — "Supervisory authority and incident-response chain" (l.1135), "Shared Security Organizations" (l.3740)
proposedGenericDecision: Replace with role 'the national private-sector CSIRT' or drop, since it is included only for 'ecosystem disambiguation' that is LU-specific.
rationale: CIRCL is explicitly introduced 'for ecosystem disambiguation' (not the University's first-line CSIRT). Its inclusion is pure Luxembourg-landscape navigation; safe to drop in a generic edition, or parameterize if a 'private-sector CSIRT' distinction is wanted.

surfaceForm: CSSF — Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (Luxembourg financial supervisor)
location: main-body-EN.tex — "Supervisory authority and incident-response chain" (l.1139)
proposedGenericDecision: Drop. Mentioned only to say it is NOT competent for the University — a Luxembourg-landscape clarification with no generic value.
rationale: CSSF appears solely to disambiguate the LU institutional ecosystem ('supervises only the financial sector, not the University'). Carries zero argumentative weight in a jurisdiction-agnostic document.

surfaceForm: Luxembourg House of Cybersecurity / NC3 (National Cybersecurity Competence Center)
location: main-body-EN.tex — SERIMA operators (l.1149), MONARC origin (l.2922)
proposedGenericDecision: Drop or fold into the generic 'national cybersecurity competence centre' role; only relevant as MONARC/SERIMA provenance.
rationale: Appears only as the provenance of MONARC and as a SERIMA co-operator — both of which are themselves being generalized/dropped. No standalone argumentative role.

surfaceForm: Project of law 8364 (PL 8364) — Luxembourg NIS2 transposition; cited with article numbers Art.2(34°), Art.11(1)(4°), Art.2(40°), Art.12(1)(2)(3), Art.20(2)
location: main-body-EN.tex — passim: Board message (l.50), Reading guide (l.466), Luxembourg context (l.561-569), "NIS2 Directive" (l.1044-1060), obligations mapping tables (l.1207-1304), Positions A-D (l.1407-1543), principlebox (l.3414), Propositions 2/8/14 (l.4046, l.4087, l.4125), Transition (l.3887-3926)
proposedGenericDecision: Replace specific PL-8364 article citations with role 'the national NIS2 transposition law' and map to the NIS2 Directive articles directly (Art.21 measures, Art.23 reporting, Art.20 management training/liability). Keep the Directive-level anchors; abstract the national-article numbering behind a parameter or footnote.
rationale: PL 8364 is the Luxembourg-specific instrument and its internal article numbering (2(34°), 11(1)(4°), 12(2)) is non-portable. The underlying obligations are NIS2 Directive obligations applicable in every Member State. A jurisdiction-mapping variable lets each adopter slot in its own transposition while the Directive-level argument stays fixed.

surfaceForm: Three cumulative legal pegs for essential-entity classification: public-administration-entity definition, 'essential regardless of size', exclusion of teaching establishments from the research-organisation track
location: main-body-EN.tex — "NIS2 Directive" (l.1050-1060), Luxembourg context (l.561-569), Positions B/C (l.1419-1484)
proposedGenericDecision: Generalize to the NIS2-Directive logic: a public research-and-teaching institution is in scope as an essential/important entity; the precise classification pegs are jurisdiction-dependent and should be expressed as 'under the applicable national transposition, the institution is classified as [essential|important]'.
rationale: The cumulative-pegs reasoning is built entirely on Luxembourg transposition article structure and a national classification letter. Other states classify universities differently (some important, not essential). This is an implicit national-transposition assumption that must be parameterized, not asserted as universal.

surfaceForm: Project of law 8307 (PL 8307) — Luxembourg CER Directive transposition; "deposited 1 September 2023"
location: main-body-EN.tex — "Concomitant CER framework" (l.1167-1176)
proposedGenericDecision: Replace with role 'the national CER-Directive transposition'. Keep the generic cross-reference (critical-entity designation auto-triggers essential status under NIS2) but drop the PL number and deposit date.
rationale: PL 8307 is the Luxembourg CER bill; the CER Directive (EU) 2022/2557 and its NIS2-linkage are EU-wide. The 'regulatory-neighbourhood completeness' point generalizes; the national bill number does not.

surfaceForm: ICRADP essential-entity classification letter "notified to the Department of Computer Science on 3 April 2026"; "confirmed by the ILR in a letter"; "notified on 3~April~2026"
location: main-body-EN.tex — Luxembourg context (l.569), "NIS2 Directive" (l.1041)
proposedGenericDecision: Drop the specific letter date and DCS-notification fact. Replace with generic 'where the national supervisory authority has classified the institution as an essential entity, ...'. The dated notification is a UL-specific event.
rationale: The 3 April 2026 letter to the Department of Computer Science is a concrete, dated, institution-specific regulatory event. It anchors the argument to UL's actual experience and cannot survive in an institution-agnostic template.

surfaceForm: Named governance bodies: "Board of Governors" / "Conseil de Gouvernance", "Rectorate", "Rector", "Faculty Council", "University Council", "\institution{Board of Governors}" macro usage
location: main-body-EN.tex — "On the nature of this report" box (l.26-28), Board message (l.111-125, l.159-167), Reading guide (l.445), ISO Clause 5 (l.2845), Executive training (l.3497, l.3502, l.3902, l.3933), DPC decision path (l.3541), ICRADP independence (l.4555, l.4590)
proposedGenericDecision: Parameterize to role-based governance shape: GOVERNING_BOARD (top body), EXECUTIVE_LEADERSHIP (rector/president office), ACADEMIC_SENATE / FACULTY_GOVERNANCE_BODIES. Provide a small glossary mapping so each adopter sets its own body names.
rationale: 'Board of Governors', 'Rectorate', 'Conseil de Gouvernance', 'Faculty Council', 'University Council' encode a specific continental-European university governance shape. US/UK adopters use Board of Trustees + Provost + Academic Senate. This is a major IMPLICIT governance-shape assumption; the document even uses an \institution{Board of Governors} macro that expands to a UL-specific term.

surfaceForm: DCS — Department of Computer Science ("hosting a Department of Computer Science whose research portfolio covers information-systems security"); used as the pilot site and as the basis for the 'duty to contribute' argument
location: main-body-EN.tex — "NIS2 Directive" duty-to-contribute (l.1067), Position D (l.1500), Safeguards (l.3501... ), Feasibility pilot (l.3842), Transition pilot (l.3906-3942)
proposedGenericDecision: Replace with role 'a computer-science / cybersecurity research unit' as the natural pilot host and as grounding for the knowledge-institution contribution duty. Drop the proper department name.
rationale: DCS is UL's actual computer-science department, used both as the concrete pilot entity and as the load-bearing premise for the 'duty of intellectual contribution to the regulator'. The argument generalizes to 'an institution hosting CS/security research', but the named department must be parameterized.

surfaceForm: SnT — Interdisciplinary Centre for Security, Reliability and Trust; named pilot site alongside DCS and the HPC team
location: main-body-EN.tex — Feasibility pilot (l.3843), Transition plan pilot row (l.3907), pilot discussion (l.3940)
proposedGenericDecision: Replace with role 'an interdisciplinary security/trust research centre' (or fold into CS_RESEARCH_UNIT). Drop the proper name.
rationale: SnT is the named UL interdisciplinary centre selected as a pilot. The pilot rationale ('entities with cybersecurity/HPC expertise validate the architecture') is generic; the specific centre name is not.

surfaceForm: "the university's HPC team" / ULHPC and MeluXina (EuroHPC); "ULHPC facility with petabyte-scale research traffic to MeluXina"
location: main-body-EN.tex — "Luxembourg status" (l.2733-2746), Feasibility pilot (l.3843), Transition pilot (l.3908, l.3941)
proposedGenericDecision: Replace ULHPC with role 'the institution's HPC facility/team'; replace MeluXina/EuroHPC concrete linkage with 'a national/European HPC resource'. Keep the Science-DMZ-substrate argument generically.
rationale: ULHPC and MeluXina are Luxembourg-specific HPC assets used as concrete evidence that the Science-DMZ 'substrate is present'. The argument (high-bandwidth research traffic justifies a Science DMZ) is generic; the named facilities are jurisdiction-bound.

surfaceForm: Luxembourg research-ecosystem partners cited as the federation rationale: LIST, LIH ("University of Luxembourg, LIST, LIH ... too small for three separate Science DMZs")
location: main-body-EN.tex — "Luxembourg status: what is already in place" (l.2762-2782)
proposedGenericDecision: Generalize the whole 'mutualised NREN-anchored Science DMZ for a small national ecosystem' subsection: replace named institutes with 'the national research-active institutions' and reframe the small-ecosystem reasoning as conditional ('where the national research base is small, an NREN-anchored federated Science DMZ is operationally rational').
rationale: LIST and LIH are named Luxembourg research institutes; the entire subsection 'Luxembourg status' is a jurisdiction-bound feasibility analysis. It encodes an implicit single-small-country assumption ('too small for three separate Science DMZs') that does not hold for larger systems and must be conditionalized.

surfaceForm: Committee for Reasonable Adjustments (the University of Luxembourg's existing committee, cited as institutional precedent for ICRADP)
location: main-body-EN.tex — "The precedent of the University of Luxembourg: the Committee for Reasonable Adjustments" (l.4499-4522)
proposedGenericDecision: Generalize to 'many universities already operate a reasonable-adjustments committee for students/staff with disabilities' (the IOA-Ombudsman and CRPD precedents already carry the argument). Drop the UL-specific 'the University already has...' framing.
rationale: This entire subsection is built on UL's own existing committee as the coherence anchor ('if the university already operates a mechanism..., extend it to digital policies'). The argument survives generically because reasonable-adjustments bodies are near-universal, but the UL-specific precedent framing must be generalized to 'institutions that already operate such a committee'.

surfaceForm: NCSS III — third National Cybersecurity Strategy (Luxembourg, approved 26 January 2018), Implementation Objective 7 (cooperation with academic/research sphere)
location: main-body-EN.tex — Luxembourg context (l.585-592), Methodology note (l.995), "National strategy hook" (l.1156-1165), Positions C.4/D (l.1495), Safeguards advocacy
proposedGenericDecision: Replace with role 'the applicable national cybersecurity strategy's academia-cooperation objective'. Keep the generic claim that the contribution aligns with the national strategy's research-cooperation goal; drop NCSS-III numbering and the 2018 date.
rationale: NCSS III Objective 7 is the Luxembourg national strategy hook used to legitimize the report's advocacy posture. Most states have a national cyber strategy with an academia-cooperation theme; the hook generalizes via a parameter but the LU-specific document/date does not.

surfaceForm: "the Luxembourg transposition of the NIS2 Directive" stated repeatedly as the operative legal basis; entire "Luxembourg-specific context" and "Luxembourg institutional landscape" sections
location: main-body-EN.tex — section heading "Reading guide: ... and the Luxembourg context" (l.438), subsection "The Luxembourg-specific context" (l.557), "Luxembourg institutional landscape" (l.1102-1198)
proposedGenericDecision: Convert these jurisdiction-bound sections into a parameterized 'National regulatory context' chapter driven by a localization table (supervisory authority, governmental CSIRT, SPOC, DPA, transposition law, notification platform, national strategy). Keep the EU-level regulatory landscape section (GDPR/NIS2/AI Act/Schrems II) fully generic.
rationale: Two entire subsections are explicitly framed as 'the Luxembourg context'. They are the densest cluster of national-transposition assumptions in the document. They should become a single parameterized national-context module so a generic suit-infrastructure-policy can be localized per jurisdiction.

surfaceForm: Jurisdiction-bound cost/feasibility framing: "a country that is among the wealthiest in the world", "the university's multi-year agreement with the State", "within typical university budgets"
location: main-body-EN.tex — "Justification and Feasibility" opening (l.3757-3775), Feasibility cost structure (l.3820-3860)
proposedGenericDecision: Generalize the wealth-of-country and 'multi-year agreement with the State' framing to neutral 'within a multi-year institutional planning cycle' / 'proportionate to institutional budget'. Drop the 'wealthiest country' rhetorical anchor.
rationale: The cost argument leans on Luxembourg-specific premises (national wealth, a state convention/multi-year agreement model). These are implicit jurisdiction-bound cost assumptions; the proportionate-investment argument itself is generic and survives once the LU framing is removed.

surfaceForm: Assumed organizational shape: "three faculties, each with departments of teaching and research, and interdisciplinary centres"; "research-only units, research-and-teaching departments, teaching/training-only components"
location: main-body-EN.tex — Introduction (l.691-696), DPC applied-to-UL (l.3581-3588), differentiated-needs note (l.1631-1636), ICRADP mission (l.4528-4534)
proposedGenericDecision: Generalize the unit taxonomy to role-based terms (research units, research-and-teaching units, teaching units, administrative services) without asserting a fixed faculty count. Drop 'three faculties' and the UL-specific entity-type breakdown framing.
rationale: 'Three faculties ... and interdisciplinary centres with strong industrial partnerships' is UL's concrete structure; the 'research-only / research-and-teaching / teaching-only' tripartite is also UL's specific organizational vocabulary. The functional distinction (missions: research/teaching/admin) is generic; the named structural shape and faculty count are institution-specific.

surfaceForm: \institution{Board of Governors} macro and \institution{...} semantic command applied to UL-specific bodies (Board of Governors, ILR, CNPD, Institut Luxembourgeois de Régulation, Luxembourg House of Cybersecurity)
proposedGenericDecision: Where \institution{} wraps a jurisdiction-specific body, replace the wrapped literal with the corresponding localization variable while keeping the semantic command. Generic institutions (EPFL, CERN, MIT, etc. in the precedent panel) keep their names.
rationale: The \institution{} macro is a semantic wrapper; the detection target is the LITERAL it expands to. Several occurrences expand to UL/LU-specific terms (Board of Governors, ILR, Institut Luxembourgeois de Régulation, CNPD), which must be parameterized; the macro itself is kept.

surfaceForm: Reference-panel institutions (MIT, Stanford, Cambridge, ETH Zurich, CMU, Michigan, CERN, Oxford, EPFL, Wisconsin-Madison, NC State, Penn State, Paris-Saclay, Sorbonne, CNRS, Rutgers) and their NRENs (RENATER, SWITCH, DFN, JANET/Jisc)
location: main-body-EN.tex — "Examples of universities with decentralised architecture" (l.2033-2453), NREN section (l.2653-2667), state-of-the-art (l.1697-2030)
proposedGenericDecision: Keep. These are external precedent institutions (Layer-5 evidence), not the adopting institution. They are the comparative evidence base and remain valid for any adopter. Note: EPFL/CERN/Paris-Saclay are framed as 'size-comparable to the University of Luxembourg' — that comparative clause should be parameterized/dropped, but the institutions themselves stay.
rationale: Named external precedents are institution-agnostic evidence and should be preserved. The ONLY institution-bound residue here is the comparison anchor 'comparable to the University of Luxembourg' (l.2061-2069), which should be parameterized; flagged separately below.

surfaceForm: Size-comparison anchors tying the precedent panel to UL: "EPFL (~12,000 students, comparable to the University of Luxembourg)", "the University of Luxembourg has more than two decades of experience", "Paris-Saclay ... regulated under the French equivalent of the Luxembourg framework"
location: main-body-EN.tex — "Relevant and Adequate Reference panel" (l.2058-2070)
proposedGenericDecision: Replace UL comparison anchors with parameterized scale ('size-comparable to the adopting institution') and a generic 'the adopting institution's track record'. Reframe 'French equivalent of the Luxembourg framework' as 'a comparable national NIS2 transposition'.
rationale: The panel's selection-criteria text repeatedly anchors comparability to UL ('comparable to the University of Luxembourg', 'the University of Luxembourg has more than two decades'). These are implicit institution-bound comparison claims embedded in otherwise-generic precedent justification.

surfaceForm: EUR amounts / EU-bound monetary thresholds: "sanctions up to EUR 10 M or 2% of annual turnover" (NIS2 essential-entity sanction)
location: main-body-EN.tex — "The European regulatory landscape" NIS2 entry (l.528)
proposedGenericDecision: Keep but tag as NIS2-Directive figure (EU-wide, jurisdiction-neutral within the EU). For a non-EU generic edition, parameterize the sanction figure. Within an EU-scope suit-infrastructure-policy, this is generic and may stay.
rationale: The EUR 10M / 2% turnover ceiling is the NIS2 Directive figure, identical across Member States — so it is EU-generic rather than UL-specific. Flagged because the task lists 'EUR amounts' explicitly; it only becomes a localization variable if the template targets non-EU jurisdictions.

surfaceForm: Luxembourg national transposition of Directive 2000/78/EC: "Law of 28 November 2006" integrating reasonable-adjustment obligation into national labour law; "ratified by ... Luxembourg"
location: main-body-EN.tex — ICRADP legal foundations (l.4184-4189), CRPD ratification note (l.4181)
proposedGenericDecision: Replace 'Law of 28 November 2006' with role 'the national transposition of Directive 2000/78/EC into labour law'. Generalize 'ratified by Luxembourg' to 'ratified by the EU and its Member States'.
rationale: The 28 November 2006 law is the Luxembourg transposition of the EU Equal Treatment Directive — a national-transposition fact stated with the country implied. The EU-level instruments (Directive 2000/78/EC, CRPD) are generic; the national implementing law must be parameterized.

surfaceForm: French-language UL body names used as the canonical form: "Conseil de Gouvernance", ICRADP French acronym "CARPN"
location: main-body-EN.tex — Executive training (l.3497), ICRADP proposal heading "(ICRADP; fr:\,CARPN)" (l.4524)
proposedGenericDecision: Drop the French body names and FR acronym; keep only the role-based English term and the generic acronym. 'Conseil de Gouvernance' folds into GOVERNING_BOARD; 'fr: CARPN' is dropped.
rationale: French-language body names ('Conseil de Gouvernance') and the FR acronym CARPN encode the Luxembourg/French linguistic-institutional context. They are redundant with the English role terms and carry no generic value.

surfaceForm: Single-campus / single-data-centre framing in the Science DMZ and zone architecture ("built at the campus perimeter", "campus network core", "Campus connection: each university connected at 10-100 Gbps")
location: main-body-EN.tex — Science DMZ principles (l.1715), architecture figure (l.3234), NREN architecture pattern (l.2709)
proposedGenericDecision: Soften 'the campus perimeter' to 'the institutional network perimeter (single- or multi-site)' so the architecture does not presuppose one campus. Multi-campus precedents (Michigan Ann Arbor/Dearborn/Flint, CERN Meyrin/Prevessin) already exist in the text and can be cited as the multi-site generalization.
rationale: The architecture language defaults to 'the campus' (single-site), an implicit assumption. It is low-severity because the Science DMZ pattern is genuinely campus-perimeter-defined and multi-site precedents are already discussed, but a fully institution-agnostic edition should not presuppose a single campus.

surfaceForm: JRES — biennial French academic-network conferences ("a major source of experience feedback")
location: main-body-EN.tex — "Shared Security Organizations" (l.3748), Proposition 12 (l.4108)
proposedGenericDecision: Generalize to 'regional/national academic-network conferences and communities' or keep as one example among the security-community list. Drop the French-specific framing if a non-Francophone edition is targeted.
rationale: JRES is a France-specific (Francophone) conference series. It sits in a list of otherwise-international communities (REN-ISAC, GEANT Security, FIRST). Low severity; generalize or keep as an example, but it carries a Francophone-jurisdiction flavour.
